messages:
alex: Heads up, mex-gdl POP is seeing a p99 jump starting ~08:10 UTC, steady for ~30m. Affected RLs on kernel_select path A->B oscillation.
priya: seeing it too, p50 ok but p95/p99 up 3-5x. Any recent deploys?
marta: no deploys to serving in the window. infra-bot: network-event: upstream provider announced route flap to /24 carrier peer at 08:08 UTC.
jon: looks like cross-pop failover to MX-CDN provider, RTT to backend increased ~60ms on impacted hosts. kvcache misses spiked at same time.
alex: profiling quick dump attached (snippet):
```
kernel_select: chosen=fast-matmul-v2 fallback=slow-matmul-v1
switch_count: 118 in 300s
avg_batch_size: 1.3 -> 0.6
kvcache_hit_rate: 86% -> 42%
prefix_cache_evictions/sec: +220%
```
priya: oh — batch size collapse + kv miss storm explains tokens/sec drop. If kernel selector is sampling to compute latency cost with small batches it might flip to slower kernel that assumes bigger batches.
marta: I see host-level CPU steal and ctx-switch jitter on a subset of nodes, could be noisy neighbor from provider VM oversubscription.
jon: traced a request path: host1 -> upstream-peer-A (good) ; after 08:08, many go host1 -> upstream-peer-B (higher queueing). TCP retransmits + inc RTT = kvcache warmups (misses) because requests land on different machine group.
samir: temporary mitigation ideas: 1) pin kernel selection to fallback policy for 10m on impacted hosts, 2) force local KV affinity for sticky routing, 3) rate-limit cross-pop failover to reduce churn. Thoughts?
alex: agree. Priya can we get a canary kernel pin on 3 hosts in the mex pool? pin reduces selector oscillation for quick test.
priya: will push kernel-pin via runtime flag to 3 hosts now: `/admin/runtime set kernel.pin=fast-matmul-v2 --hosts mex-gdl-0{2,5,7}`
priya: done. watching.
jon: also opened a peering ticket with provider (tkt#PR-4498) — they confirm brief congestion during 08:05-08:20 and route flap handling.
priya: p99 down to ~baseline after pinning but kvcache hit rate recovering slower. Might need kvcache warmup pressure relief (backfill or prefetch).
marta: started a controlled prefetch job for hot prefixes on impacted hosts, low QPS backfill.
jon: infra-bot: route-update resolved with provider at 08:22 UTC.
alex: will keep running prefills for 20m and monitor. Also capture full perf trace for later root cause.
samir: please capture perf.data + kernel_trace and put in /mnt/ops/2112349999-mex-gdl for postmortem.
priya: uploaded perf trace and selector logs: /mnt/ops/2112349999-mex-gdl/{perf.data,selector.log,kvcache-metrics.csv}
priya: (typo) priya: uploaded...
jon: initial quick-read shows selector sampling window shrank under high RTT variance which increased variance in estimated cost -> more frequent flips. We'll look at making selector hysteresis stronger on unstable network signals.
marta: note for postmortem: chain of events = provider route flap -> cross-pop failover -> RTT/queueing up -> kvcache miss storm (loss of affinity) -> kernel selector oscillation -> batch collapse -> p99 spike.
alex: agreed. Timeline saved. Assigning follow-ups: priya (kernel selector hysteresis tweak), jon (peering SLA follow-up + provider mitigation), marta (kvcache prefill/backfill logic), samir (write up incident).
samir: I'll draft a short postmortem and include traces + mitigations. ETA 24h.
alex: thanks all. We'll keep this thread open until postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:
